method: Fully contained intervals only; time-weight sample spans. For each span, count streams whose cumulative application body bytes increased. Rate equals the fraction of time with progress times the mean progressing stream count during that time times delivered MiB per progressing stream-second. Grouping 2 or 4 consecutive native spans also counts streams which advanced in different parts of that longer span. Retain the last partial group; bytes and endpoints are identical at each resolution.
population: All 3 release diagnostic sets across all 4 arms with 160 sequential fresh requests per arm. Candidate is the published release path; direct is guest DNAT. The third OrbStack context run retains one reopened bulk stream. All 4 fixed-duration diagnostic sets retain bulk and mixed runs. The fourth mixed run overlapped profiler attachment and is outside the three clean-set interpretation.
limitations: Observed application delivery does not identify kqueue readiness, worker assignment, simultaneous CPU service, network packet timing or cause. Replacing idle spans at observed nonidle rate is a conditional arithmetic comparison. The paths are sequential observations and have different achieved fresh arrival rates. Older 6.18.35 guest path traces cannot establish throughput on the current four-vCPU holdout.
